title: Regulatory Approval Is Not Enough: Gaps in Trustworthy AI Reporting in FDA-Cleared Medical Devices
abstract: arXiv:2608.12360v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Background: AI/ML-enabled medical devices are increasingly deployed in healthcare under evolving regulatory frameworks. As these systems become more integrated into clinical decision-making, there is growing expectation that they demonstrate key dimensions of trustworthy AI to support clinician, patient, and public trust. Whether publicly available regulatory documentation provides sufficient evidence to independently assess the trustworthiness of cleared AI systems remains unclear. Methods: We analysed FDA AI/ML-enabled medical device summary reports published between 2021 and 2025. Reports underwent automated keyword screening followed by multi-stage manual consensus review to identify documented evidence for the six FUTURE-AI principles: Fairness, Universality, Traceability, Usability, Robustness, and Explainability. translated_title: 监管批准还不够：FDA批准的医疗器械中可信AI报告的空白
translated_abstract: 摘要：在不断演变的监管框架下，AI/ML驱动的医疗器械正越来越多地部署在医疗保健领域。随着这些系统更深入地融入临床决策，人们日益期望它们展现可信AI的关键维度，以支持临床医生、患者和公众的信任。然而，公开可用的监管文件是否提供了足够证据，以独立评估已批准AI系统的可信度，仍不清楚。方法：我们分析了2021年至2025年间发布的FDA AI/ML医疗器械摘要报告。报告经过自动关键词筛选，随后进行多阶段手动共识审查，以识别FUTURE-AI六项原则（公平性、普遍性、可追溯性、可用性、稳健性和可解释性）的文档化证据。进行了描述性、时间性和临床领域分析。多变量逻辑回归评估了是否...
tldr: 该研究分析了FDA批准的AI医疗器械报告，发现监管文件在记录可信AI原则方面存在显著空白，仅依赖监管批准不足以评估系统的可信度。
en_tdlr: This study analyzed FDA-cleared AI medical device reports and found significant gaps in documenting trustworthy AI principles, indicating that regulatory approval alone is insufficient for assessing system trustworthiness.
